title: Sales Engineers
description: Sell business goods or services, the selling of which requires a technical background equivalent to a baccalaureate degree in engineering.

tasks.text: Develop, present, or respond to proposals for specific customer requirements, including request for proposal responses and industry-specific solutions.
Collaborate with sales teams to understand customer requirements, to promote the sale of company products, and to provide sales support.
Create sales or service contracts for products or services.
Visit prospective buyers at commercial, industrial, or other establishments to show samples or catalogs, and to inform them about product pricing, availability, and advantages.
Keep informed on industry news and trends, products, services, competitors, relevant information about legacy, existing, and emerging technologies, and the latest product-line developments.
Identify resale opportunities and support them to achieve sales plans.
Confer with customers and engineers to assess equipment needs and to determine system requirements.
Plan and modify product configurations to meet customer needs.
Prepare and deliver technical presentations that explain products or services to customers and prospective customers.
Recommend improved materials or machinery to customers, documenting how such changes will lower costs or increase production.
Maintain sales forecasting reports.
Document account activities, generate reports, and keep records of business transactions with customers and suppliers.
Research and identify potential customers for products or services.
Secure and renew orders and arrange delivery.
Develop sales plans to introduce products in new markets.
Attend trade shows and seminars to promote products or to learn about industry developments.
Attend company training seminars to become familiar with product lines.
Arrange for demonstrations or trial installations of equipment.
Train team members in the customer applications of technologies.
Sell products requiring extensive technical expertise and support for installation and use, such as material handling equipment, numerical-control machinery, or computer systems.
Provide information needed for the development of custom-made machinery.
Provide technical and non-technical support and services to clients or other staff members regarding the use, operation, and maintenance of equipment.
Diagnose problems with installed equipment.
Write technical documentation for products.
Report to supervisors about prospective firms' credit ratings.

skills.name: Speaking
skills.def: Talking to others to convey information effectively.

skills.name: Persuasion
skills.def: Persuading others to change their minds or behavior.

skills.name: Reading Comprehension
skills.def: Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents.

skills.name: Active Listening
skills.def: Giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times.

skills.name: Critical Thinking
skills.def: Using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions, or approaches to problems.

skills.name: Social Perceptiveness
skills.def: Being aware of others' reactions and understanding why they react as they do.

skills.name: Judgment and Decision Making
skills.def: Considering the relative costs and benefits of potential actions to choose the most appropriate one.

skills.name: Negotiation
skills.def: Bringing others together and trying to reconcile differences.

skills.name: Complex Problem Solving
skills.def: Identifying complex problems and reviewing related information to develop and evaluate options and implement solutions.

skills.name: Writing
skills.def: Communicating effectively in writing as appropriate for the needs of the audience.

skills.name: Active Learning
skills.def: Understanding the implications of new information for both current and future problem-solving and decision-making.

skills.name: Service Orientation
skills.def: Actively looking for ways to help people.

skills.name: Systems Analysis
skills.def: Determining how a system should work and how changes in conditions, operations, and the environment will affect outcomes.

skills.name: Systems Evaluation
skills.def: Identifying measures or indicators of system performance and the actions needed to improve or correct performance, relative to the goals of the system.

skills.name: Time Management
skills.def: Managing one's own time and the time of others.

skills.name: Coordination
skills.def: Adjusting actions in relation to others' actions.

skills.name: Instructing
skills.def: Teaching others how to do something.

skills.name: Mathematics
skills.def: Using mathematics to solve problems.

skills.name: Learning Strategies
skills.def: Selecting and using training/instructional methods and procedures appropriate for the situation when learning or teaching new things.

skills.name: Monitoring
skills.def: Monitoring/Assessing performance of yourself, other individuals, or organizations to make improvements or take corrective action.

skills.name: Data base user interface and query software
skills.def: Software to query, present, or edit information stored in a database sytem. Examples: Amazon Web Services AWS software, Database management software, IBM DB2, Microsoft Access.

skills.name: Object or component oriented development software
skills.def: Software to create or maintain applications using object-oriented programming concepts. Examples: C++, Oracle Java, Perl, Python.

skills.name: Development environment software
skills.def: Software to create or maintain applications which run on a computer or mobile device. Examples: C, Microsoft Azure software, Ruby.

skills.name: Office suite software
skills.def: Software to provide word processing, spreadsheet, e-mail, presentations, or data management capabilities. Examples: Google Workspace software, Microsoft Office software.

skills.name: Customer relationship management CRM software
skills.def: Software to manage customer interactions. Examples: Microsoft Dynamics, Salesforce software.

skills.name: Presentation software
skills.def: Software to create presentations, speeches, or slideshows. Examples: Microsoft PowerPoint, WebEx Sales Center.
